items.title: Falcon: the Serving add-on

labels.name: falcon
labels.description: The Falcon: the platform on one VM (deploy/compose, deploy/thalassa)

items.body:
### The problem

The base Falcon shows data only through the Crows Nest. Teams that want self-service BI, or that
already use Power BI, need their own tools on the data. Those tools cannot attach the lake: the
catalog is SQLite on the VM. And letting tools attach DuckDB directly would bring three problems:

1. **No sandbox.** A BI tool's SQL screen runs any DuckDB SQL, so
   `SELECT * FROM read_text('/srv/falcon/<project>/.env')` reads the project's secrets.
2. **DuckDB version coupling.** Each tool brings its own DuckDB; every toolkit upgrade becomes an
   upgrade of every tool.
3. **Logins** per tool, outside the Falcon's control.

### Proposed change

**The Falcon stops at a serving database; the customer chooses and runs the tools.**

- **Postgres** as an optional service: `falcon: serving: true` in `datavloot.yml`, rendered by
  `datavloot upgrade` (#55).
- A Dagster asset after `dbt build` copies the business layer into it (it reads the lake and
  writes to Postgres, not to the lake). Business layer only; a full copy per run is fine at
  small-team volumes, incremental later if needed.
- A **read-only user per consumer** (per tool, or per person), created with a `datavloot`
  command or documented SQL. Postgres's own permissions do the sandbox's work: `SELECT` on the
  business schemas, nothing else.
- **Network**, a setting per customer:

  | Level | How | When |
  |---|---|---|
  | `internal` | Only the VM's Docker network | Tools the customer runs on the VM itself |
  | `vpn` | Reachable over a private network: WireGuard, Tailscale, or a site-to-site VPN to the customer's network. Closed to the internet | **The recommended way.** Power BI Desktop and laptops connect directly; the Power BI gateway runs in the customer's network |
  | `public` | Port 5432 with TLS, an allowlist **on the load balancer or the security group** | Last resort. An allowlist on the VM does not work: the Thalassa load balancer hides the client's IP (seen as `10.20.1.2` in the oauth2-proxy logs, vlootplan A3), unless the PROXY protocol is set up |

- **Not in conflict with D7**: D7 is about where the lake's catalog lives; this is a serving copy.
  Record it in the fleet ADR so the two are not confused.
- **Out of scope:** hosting the customer's tools. We document how to connect Power BI, and
  check whether the Power BI Service needs an on-premises data gateway for a Postgres that is not
  on Azure (likely yes).

Considered and set aside: a live protocol gateway in front of DuckDB (Postgres wire: BuenaVista;
Arrow Flight SQL: GizmoSQL). No copy, but young projects, and the sandbox has to be rebuilt
inside it. Revisit if customers need real-time data.

### Things to tell the customer

- Their tools sign in with Postgres users, not through their IdP: a second set of accounts, to
  rotate and revoke.
- Data leaves the VM into their tools (Power BI datasets, laptops). Their choice, but it changes
  the "data stays on the VM" story.
- Freshness: the serving copy is as fresh as the last Dagster run.

### Acceptance criteria

- With `serving: true` and `datavloot upgrade`, the Falcon runs a Postgres that holds the business
  layer after a Dagster run.
- A consumer user can `SELECT` the business layer and nothing else; `pg_read_file` and writes are
  refused.
- With `internal` and `vpn`, port 5432 is not reachable from the internet (same check as T6 in the
  vlootplan).
- The Falcon README has a Power BI guide for the `vpn` level.
- Without the add-on, no Postgres runs.

items.title: ROADMAP: Docs and deferred research
items.body:
# ROADMAP: Docs and deferred research

## Purpose

A single long-running issue that bundles documentation work and deferred research. Each item here is intentionally not its own issue — either because it's small enough to absorb incrementally, or because it's a research topic whose scope depends on other issues' outcomes.

Close items by checking them off, not by closing the issue. The issue closes only when all items are addressed or explicitly deprecated.

---

## Section 1: Layer behavior specifications (DOCS)

Write reference documentation that captures what each layer does, configurable options, and naming conventions. These docs sit in `docs/layers/` and are referenced from the main README.

### 1.1 Silver layer specification — `docs/layers/silver.md`

- [ ] Purpose: cleaning, typing, aliasing, SCD application, DQ flagging, timezone normalization
- [ ] Organization options: `per_source_schema` (default), `per_source_schema + unified`, `single_schema`
- [ ] Naming conventions:
  - Schema: `<source_db_lower>` (from the source_db field)
  - Table: `<alias>` (from the alias field)
  - Full: `silver.<source_db_lower>.<alias>`
- [ ] Column conventions: `_loaded_at`, `_source_ts`, `_source_timezone`, `_dq_status`, `_dq_reason`, `_valid_from`/`_valid_to`/`_sk` for Type 2 dimensions, `snapshot_date` for periodic snapshots
- [ ] Consumption guidance: who should query silver directly, when to build a view, when to promote to gold
- [ ] Worked example using rama_dw

### 1.2 Gold layer specification — `docs/layers/gold.md`

- [ ] Purpose: subject-area conformed facts and dimensions; consumer-facing
- [ ] Organization: `subject_schema` (default: `gold.sales`, `gold.product`, `gold.finance`), optional `audience_schema` for mart-per-consumer
- [ ] Kimball bus architecture: conformed dimensions (product, location, customer, time) shared across facts
- [ ] Mart pattern: views over subject tables, not duplicated data
- [ ] When to escalate a mart to its own schema (access control boundaries)
- [ ] Worked example using rama_dw (unified product dimension across SAP + ZAKYA)

### 1.3 Bronze layer specification — `docs/layers/bronze.md`

- [ ] Purpose: source-faithful capture, append-only, never transformed
- [ ] File organization options (reference issue #3)
- [ ] Source naming preserved (typos, spaces, mixed case all kept as-is)
- [ ] No DQ checks at bronze — rows always land, errors surface in silver
- [ ] Archive strategy (DuckDB → Parquet export for long-term retention)

### 1.4 Manifest file organization — `docs/manifest-file-org.md`

- [ ] When single `curation.json` is sufficient (< 100 entries)
- [ ] Migration path to directory-per-source as entry count grows
- [ ] Generator merge semantics when manifest is split across files
- [ ] Example directory structure for enterprise client (11+ sources)

---

## Section 2: Deferred research items

These are real problems without obvious solutions. Each needs a research pass before an implementation issue can be filed.

### 2.1 Cross-system product entity resolution

**Problem:** Unified `gold.product` requires mapping SAP MATNR ↔ ZAKYA item_id ↔ Gofrugal product code. No client has this mapping table today. Options:

- Fuzzy match on EAN/barcode columns (high precision, requires EAN column in all sources)
- Fuzzy match on product name (lower precision, high recall)
- Manual curation interface (spreadsheet-based; doesn't scale)
- Tools: Zingg, Splink, or commercial entity resolution services

**Deliverable:** Decision doc in `docs/research/entity-resolution.md` with recommended approach, POC code, and confidence scoring design.

**Status:** Not started

### 2.2 Orchestration DAG derivation

**Problem:** Once silver/gold SQL is generated, the pipeline needs to know load order and parallelism opportunities. Options:

- Parse generated SQL for `FROM`/`JOIN` references (like dbt does)
- Require explicit `depends_on` in manifest (rejected — user already vetoed this)
- Use `group` field as DAG hint (simple; loses granularity)

**Deliverable:** DAG derivation implementation reading generated SQL. Reference: dbt's node parsing, sqlmesh's dependency detection.

**Status:** Not started

### 2.3 Surrogate key propagation

**Problem:** SCD Type 2 dimensions get `_sk` (surrogate keys). Facts joining those dimensions should join on `_sk`, not natural key, to get historically-correct dimension state. Today facts join on natural key only.

**Deliverable:** Design for `sk_join` option in fact table config. Must preserve the ability to join by natural key for use cases that want "current state" rather than "historical state."

**Status:** Not started — low priority until a client actually uses SCD Type 2.

### 2.4 Column-level curation

**Problem:** `curation.json` is table-level. Some classifications are column-level: PII flags, monetary columns requiring extra precision, derived columns that should be dropped in silver.

**Options:**
- Extend curation.json with a `columns` object per entry (we removed this in v1 for YAGNI; may need to add back)
- Separate `columns.yaml` (like checks.yaml in issue #9)
- Auto-derive from schema JSONs + heuristics (e.g., column name patterns for PII)

**Deliverable:** Design doc + decision.

**Status:** Not started

### 2.5 Accumulating snapshot history retention

**Problem:** Accumulating snapshots (order lifecycle) update rows in place, losing history of stage progression. Some clients will want full history.

See issue #6. `versioned` history strategy deferred — this is where it gets designed.

**Status:** Deferred until client request.

### 2.6 Multi-timezone column support

**Problem:** Issue #8 handles timezone at source-system level. Some tables have per-row timezone (global POS with per-store timezone). Requires column-level timezone declaration.

**Status:** Deferred until client hits this.

### 2.7 Grain validation for fact joins

**Problem:** When silver produces a fact table at one grain and gold joins it with another, mismatched grain silently produces wrong totals. Could the `grain` field drive validation that catches this at generation time?

**Deliverable:** Research spike — is grain-based join validation feasible without being annoying? What's the false positive rate?

**Status:** Not started

### 2.8 MotherDuck / cloud DuckDB support

**Problem:** Local DuckDB is single-writer; MotherDuck removes this constraint. Some enterprise clients may want cloud-hosted. How do bronze file organization and ATTACH patterns translate?

**Deliverable:** Document MotherDuck-specific patterns and any code changes required.

**Status:** Not started

---

## Section 3: Cross-cutting housekeeping

- [ ] Naming convention document: table names, column names, schema names, file names across all layers
- [ ] Migration guide: moving a client from v1 curation manifest to v2
- [ ] Example gallery: small client (rama_dw), medium, enterprise (sanitized from real deployments)
- [ ] Generator extensibility: how to add a custom transform for a custom table_type

---

## How to use this issue

1. When picking up an item, leave a comment with start date and intended scope.
2. When completing an item, check it off and link the PR or document commit.
3. If an item grows beyond its scope during work, split it into a dedicated issue and remove from here.
4. Review quarterly — items that haven't moved in 6 months either need priority or should be deprecated.

+| schemas | `bronze`, `silver`, `gold` | `shop-01-bronze`, `shop-02-silver`, `shop-03-gold` | one schema in each catalog |
+| bronze | `bronze` | `shop-04-customers`, `shop-05-products`, `shop-06-lines` | the two small seed tables and the generated order lines |
+| silver | `silver` | `shop-07-stg-cust`, `shop-08-stg-prod`, `shop-09-stg-lines` | three views with clean names and types |
+| gold | `gold` | `shop-10-revenue`, `shop-11-ltv`, `shop-12-mix` | `daily_revenue`, `customer_ltv` (window functions), `product_mix` |
+
+A pipeline runs exactly one statement, so every step of the shop is one pipeline; they run in name order, and the number in the
+name is that order. Nothing is downloaded and nothing large is stored in Git: the order lines are built inside the query engine
+from the line number (`scale` of them, a multiple of 1000, default 200 000).
+
+## Before you start (an administrator, once)
+
+- The catalogs `bronze`, `silver` and `gold` exist, and the group named in `bundle.yaml` (`ownerGroup: demo`) has a pipeline
+  principal (`pipeline-demo`) that may write to them. In the platform repository: `make demo-access GROUP=demo`. For another
+  group, change `ownerGroup` and `runAs` in `bundle.yaml`.
+- You are a member of that group and have signed in: `stardelt login`.
+
+## The loop
+
+```bash
+cd examples/shop-bundle
+stardelt bundle validate .            # offline: twelve pipelines for each of the two targets
+stardelt bundle plan . -t dev         # twelve lines "would-create"
+stardelt bundle deploy . -t dev       # twelve pipelines, named dev-<your name>-shop-NN-..., no schedule
+stardelt bundle run . -t dev          # starts them one after the other, waits for each, stops at the first that fails
+stardelt bundle summary . -t dev      # what runs on the stage, from which commit
+```
+
+Then look at the results in the **SQL editor** (the tables of the `dev` target live in the schema `shop_dev`):
+
+```sql
+select * from gold.shop_dev.daily_revenue order by order_date desc limit 7;
+select * from gold.shop_dev.customer_ltv order by value_rank limit 10;
+select * from gold.shop_dev.product_mix order by revenue desc limit 10;
+```
+
+Every statement of the run is in your **Query log** with the source "Pipeline task". The **Deployments** page shows the bundle, the
+target, the commit and who deployed it.
+
+Change something (for example the `scale` variable in `bundle.yaml`), then:
+
+```bash
+stardelt bundle plan . -t dev --diff  # shows what would change in each pipeline
+stardelt bundle deploy . -t dev
+stardelt bundle run . -t dev --only shop-06-lines
+```
+
+`--only` takes the name with or without the `dev-<your name>-` prefix. After `scale` changed, run the pipelines from `shop-06-lines`
+on again (the tables downstream are rebuilt from the lines).
+
+## The two targets
+
+- `dev` (mode `development`): your own copy, pipelines named `dev-<your name>-shop-NN-...`, no schedule, tables in the schema
+  `shop_dev`. Pipeline names of a development copy are limited to 40 characters, so a sign-in name of up to 18 characters fits.
+- `prod` (mode `production`, `runAs: pipeline-demo`): the shared copy an administrator publishes once, pipelines named
+  `shop-NN-...`, tables in the schema `shop`. It has no schedule either; run it with `stardelt bundle run . -t prod`.
+
+## Take it down
+
+`stardelt bundle destroy . -t dev --yes` removes the pipelines. The tables stay (a pipeline cannot be told to drop what it made);
+drop them in the SQL editor, one statement at a time:
+
+```sql
+drop view silver.shop_dev.stg_order_lines;
+drop view silver.shop_dev.stg_products;
+drop view silver.shop_dev.stg_customers;
+drop table gold.shop_dev.product_mix;
+drop table gold.shop_dev.customer_ltv;
+drop table gold.shop_dev.daily_revenue;
+drop table bronze.shop_dev.order_lines;
+drop table bronze.shop_dev.products;
+drop table bronze.shop_dev.customers;
+drop schema gold.shop_dev;
+drop schema silver.shop_dev;
+drop schema bronze.shop_dev;
+```
+
+## How it differs from the dbt version
+
+- No tests (dbt's twenty tests have no counterpart in a plain pipeline), and `daily_revenue` is rebuilt on every run instead of
+  merging the last three days.
+- Seeds are `values` lists inside two statements (`sql/04_customers.sql`, `sql/05_products.sql`), generated from the CSV files of
+  `examples/shop/seeds`.
+- The statements were checked for syntax only (parsed with the Trino dialect) and the bundle with `stardelt bundle validate`.

+  and a failure is a bug in this example, file it. Times and memory are recorded here after that run, never guessed.

+-- The compute of the example: ${params.scale} order lines built inside the query engine, nothing downloaded and
+-- nothing stored in Git. `sequence` is limited to 10 000 entries, so the numbers come from two small sequences
+-- (blocks of 1000 times 1000); ${params.scale} must be a multiple of 1000. Customer, product, quantity and day come
+-- from a hash of the line number: the same lines every run.
+create or replace table bronze.${params.schema}.order_lines as
+with blocks as (
+    select x from unnest(sequence(0, ${params.scale} / 1000 - 1)) as t(x)
+),
+within_block as (
+    select y from unnest(sequence(1, 1000)) as t(y)
+),
+numbered as (
+    select x * 1000 + y as order_line_id from blocks cross join within_block
+)

+    order_line_id,
+    1 + mod(mod(from_big_endian_64(xxhash64(to_utf8('c' || cast(order_line_id as varchar)))), 200) + 200, 200) as customer_id,
+    1 + mod(mod(from_big_endian_64(xxhash64(to_utf8('p' || cast(order_line_id as varchar)))), 30) + 30, 30) as product_id,

items.title: [Bug] BigQuery: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES relation discovery fails on hidden (_-prefixed) datasets

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: A defect: dbt behaves incorrectly versus expected/reference behavior.

labels.name: adapter:bigquery
labels.description: Concerns the BigQuery adapter / SQL dialect.

labels.name: area:adapters
labels.description: The adapter framework/layer connecting dbt to warehouses (dbt-adapter* crates).

items.body:
### Is this a new bug in dbt Fusion?

- [x] I believe this is a new bug in dbt Fusion
- [x] I have searched the existing issues and could not find a duplicate

### Current Behavior

dbt Fusion's `bigquery_v1` adapter performs relation discovery and existence checks by issuing SQL queries of the form:

```sql
SELECT table_catalog, table_schema, table_name, table_type
FROM `{project}`.`{schema}`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
WHERE table_name = '{model}';
```

BigQuery does not expose hidden datasets (those whose names start with `_`) via `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`. When the target schema is `_`-prefixed, BigQuery returns:

```
dbt1308: [BigQuery] googleapi: Error 400: Cannot use INFORMATION_SCHEMA with a hidden dataset: {_schema}, invalid
```

This affects at least four code paths in the adapter:

1. **Bulk deferral hydration** — startup query against `{project}.{_schema}.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`
2. **Per-model existence check** — `WHERE table_name = '{model}'` lookup during `is_incremental()` evaluation and the drop/recreate path
3. **Per-seed existence check** — same lookup issued for each seed before materialization
4. **`catalog.json` generation** — large join across `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES`, `MATERIALIZED_VIEWS`, `TABLE_OPTIONS`, `COLUMNS`, `COLUMN_FIELD_PATHS` against the hidden schema

Neither `static_analysis: 'off'` nor `--no-introspect` suppresses these runtime lookups.

### Expected Behavior

dbt Fusion should successfully discover relations and run incremental models, seeds, and catalog generation against `_`-prefixed (hidden) BigQuery datasets, matching the behavior of `dbt-core`'s BigQuery adapter.

`dbt-core` solved the equivalent problem in 2018 by switching to the BigQuery REST API (`client.list_datasets(include_all=True)` and `projects.datasets.tables.list`), which supports hidden datasets. See [dbt-core PR dbt-labs/dbt-core#13978](https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/pull/1006).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Configure a BigQuery target.
2. Add a `generate_schema_name` macro that returns the custom schema name as-is (mirrors the common production pattern where schemas are set directly in `dbt_project.yml`):

   ```jinja
   {% macro generate_schema_name(custom_schema_name, node) -%}
       {%- if custom_schema_name is none -%}
           {{ target.schema }}
       {%- else -%}
           {{ custom_schema_name | trim }}
       {%- endif -%}
   {%- endmacro %}
   ```

3. Create a minimal incremental model targeting a hidden dataset:

   ```sql
   {{
       config(
           materialized='incremental',
           schema='_repro_hidden',
           unique_key='id',
           incremental_strategy='merge',
           full_refresh=false
       )
   }}

   select 1 as id, current_timestamp() as updated_at

   {% if is_incremental() %}
       where updated_at > (select max(updated_at) from {{ this }})
   {% endif %}
   ```

4. Run:

   ```bash
   dbt run --full-refresh
   ```

5. Observe failure with `Error 400: Cannot use INFORMATION_SCHEMA with a hidden dataset: _repro_hidden`.

> **Note:** `--full-refresh` (or running against an already-existing relation in a hidden schema) is required to trigger the existence-check code path. A first-time green-field `dbt run` short-circuits the lookup and masks the bug.

### Relevant log output

```shell
dbt-fusion 2.0.0-preview.176
   Loading profiles.yml
   Loading packages.yml
    Failed [  2.57s] model _repro_hidden.table_hidden_schema (table)
    Failed [  4.78s] model _repro_hidden.incremental_hidden_schema (incremental)

error: dbt1308: Database Error in model table_hidden_schema
  [BigQuery] googleapi: Error 400: Cannot use INFORMATION_SCHEMA with a hidden dataset: _repro_hidden, invalid
error: dbt1308: [BigQuery] googleapi: Error 400: Cannot use INFORMATION_SCHEMA with a hidden dataset: _repro_hidden, invalid
  (in models/repro/zd_121109_hidden_dataset_information_schema/incremental_hidden_schema.sql:31:7)
```

Customer-side per-model failing query (captured from dbt platform run log):

```sql
SELECT table_catalog,
       table_schema,
       table_name,
       table_type
FROM `{project}`.`_int`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES
WHERE table_name = 'int_web_sessions';
```

### Environment

- OS: macOS (also reproduced on dbt platform hosted Fusion, Linux)
- CPU: ARM (local repro), x86 (dbt platform)
- dbt Fusion: 2.0.0-preview.175 and 2.0.0-preview.176
- Adapter + version: bigquery_v1

### Which database adapter are you using?

- [x] bigquery

### Is this a discrepancy vs. dbt Core?

- [x] Yes — this works in dbt Core but not dbt Fusion

`dbt-core`'s BigQuery adapter uses the BigQuery REST API (`include_all=True`) for relation discovery, which supports hidden datasets. The same project runs green on `dbt-core` and fails on `dbt-fusion`.

### Additional Context

**Related issues and prior work:**
- dbt-core dbt-labs/dbt-core#13865 — dbt errors on BigQuery datasets beginning with underscores (closed 2018): https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/873
- dbt-core PR dbt-labs/dbt-core#13978 — fix using `client.list_datasets(include_all=True)`: https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/pull/1006
- dbt-fusion dbt-labs/dbt-core#13508 — Fusion slower when querying information_schema (open): https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt-core/issues/13508

**Suggested fixes (in priority order):**
1. Use the BigQuery REST API (`projects.datasets.tables.list` with `include_all=true`) for relation discovery — mirrors the `dbt-core` fix and supports hidden datasets natively.
2. Use BigQuery's legacy `__TABLES__` meta-view — works on hidden datasets.
3. Catch the 400 "hidden dataset" error and fall back to "relation state unknown" (proceed as first-run / merge-as-if-table-exists).

**Workarounds currently in use:**
- Renamed hidden schemas to non-hidden (`_stg` → `stg`, `_int` → `int`, `_seeds` → `seeds`) where possible.
- For schemas that must remain hidden, removed `is_incremental()` and replaced with unconditional rolling-window filters + `full_refresh=false`. Trade-off: no auto-catch-up.

**Customer impact:** Blocks an Enterprise migration from `dbt-core` to `dbt-fusion`.

items.title: Issue 1 — Build Gold Dimensions: `dim_location` & `dim_customers`

## Description
Create two Gold-layer dimensions to model customer entities and their locations. `dim_location` should uniquely represent a location; `dim_customers` should contain one row per customer and reference `dim_location`.

## Scope
- Gold schema only.
- No SQL/YAML implementation in this issue body (handled in PR).
- Uses Silver inputs (`stg_customers`).

## Deliverables
- `models/gold/dimensions/dim_location.sql`
- `models/gold/dimensions/dim_customers.sql`
- Entries in `models/gold/schema.yml` for both models with tests (uniqueness, not_null, relationships).
- Model docs (description blocks).

## Tasks
1. Create feature branch: `feature/gold-dim-location-customers`.
2. Add model files and schema tests (no SQL in issue; implement in code).
3. Ensure clear grain:
   1. `dim_location`: one row per unique location.
   2. `dim_customers`: one row per customer, includes `location_id`.
4. Add column-level descriptions in `schema.yml`.
5. Run `dbt build --select dim_location dim_customers` in the PR checks.
6. Open PR, request 2 reviewers from `@phoenix-team2/dbt-reviewers`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Models compile and run successfully in Gold.
- [ ] Tests pass:
  - [ ] `dim_location.location_id` is `unique` and `not_null`.
  - [ ] `dim_customers.customer_id` is `unique` and `not_null`.
  - [ ] `dim_customers.location_id` has a `relationships` test to `dim_location.location_id`.
- [ ] PR approved by two reviewers and merged.

## Dependencies
- Silver: `stg_customers`.
